name: Texas
note: The funeral director files the death certificate electronically with the local registrar within 10 days, after the attending physician, PA or APRN, or for reportable deaths the justice of the peace or medical examiner, completes the medical certification within five days of receiving it. From the vital statistics unit the death reaches the Secretary of State weekly for the voter roll, while local registrars send monthly abstracts to county voter registrars; DSHS also supplies DPS and certain hospitals, and HHSC matches the death records monthly against Medicaid, TANF and SNAP. Certified copies are restricted to qualified applicants, and death records become public 25 years after death. The inquest law in Code of Criminal Procedure chapter 49 is recodified as chapter 49A from 1 April 2027.

citations.title: Standard used in determining death
citations.quote: A registered nurse, including an advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant may determine and pronounce a person dead

citations.title: Deaths requiring an inquest
citations.quote: A justice of the peace shall conduct an inquest into the death of a person who dies in the county served by the justice if:

citations.title: Notification of investigating official
citations.quote: A peace officer who has been notified of the death of a person whose death requires an inquest under Article 49.04

citations.title: Orders and death certificates
citations.quote: The justice of the peace or other person who conducts an inquest under this subchapter shall sign the death certificate

citations.title: Medical examiners

citations.cite: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 49A.053 (effective 1 April 2027)

citations.quote: the person dies by suicide or the circumstances of the death indicate that the death may have been caused by suicide

citations.title: Time and place for filing death certificate
citations.quote: Not later than the 10th day after the date of a death that occurs in this state, a death certificate shall be filed

citations.title: Personal and medical information
citations.quote: The person required to file a death certificate shall obtain the required personal information from a competent person with knowledge of the facts.

citations.title: Medical certification (catchline: Personal information)
citations.quote: The attending physician, physician assistant, or advanced practice registered nurse shall complete the medical certification not later than five days after receiving the death certificate.

citations.title: Electronic medical certification

citations.title: Burial-transit permit

citations.title: Assuming custody of body

citations.title: Report of death as authority to transport or bury

citations.title: Waiting period for cremation
citations.quote: A crematory establishment may not cremate human remains within 48 hours of the time of death indicated on a death certificate

citations.title: Body disinterred or cremated

citations.title: Certified copies

citations.quote: The registrar shall cancel a voter's registration immediately on receipt of:

steps.title: Death is determined and pronounced by a physician, or by a nurse or physician assistant under facility policy
steps.who: A physician; a registered nurse (including an APRN) or physician assistant may determine and pronounce death if the written policies of the licensed facility or entity caring for the person permit it. Brain-death determinations (§ 671.001(b)) remain with a physician.
steps.summary: Health and Safety Code § 671.001 sets the standard for death. Subsection (d) lets registered nurses, APRNs and physician assistants pronounce death, other than on brain-death criteria, where facility policies allow; death must be pronounced before artificial support is withdrawn.

steps.title: Justice of the peace or medical examiner holds an inquest into a reportable death
steps.who: A physician or other person in possession of the body, and any peace officer notified of the death, must immediately notify the justice of the peace; in a county with a medical examiner, deaths are reported to that office, to which the justices' inquest powers pass.
steps.trigger: Deaths in prison or jail, unnatural deaths, bodies found with unknown cause or identity, suspected unlawful means or suicide, deaths without a physician in attendance, deaths a physician cannot certify, and certain child deaths (art. 49.04; art. 49.25 § 6 in medical-examiner counties).
steps.summary: Justices of the peace are the inquest officers except where a county has a medical examiner (art. 49.25 § 12). The person conducting the inquest signs the death certificate. Chapter 49 is repealed and recodified as chapter 49A with effect from 1 April 2027 (H.B. 1610, 2025), with the same list of inquest deaths.

steps.title: Attending physician, PA or APRN, or the inquest officer, completes the medical certification within five days
steps.who: The decedent's attending physician, or a physician assistant or APRN who treated the condition that contributed to death; if they are unavailable and approve, an associate physician, the institution's chief medical officer or the autopsy physician in natural deaths. In inquest cases, the person conducting the inquest.
steps.trigger: The person filing the certificate (the funeral director) presents the death certificate for medical certification.

deadline.text: not later than five days after receiving the death certificate

steps.summary: The certifier attests electronically through a process approved by the state registrar (§ 193.005(h)). If the certification is delayed the certifier must tell the funeral director why, and the body may not be disposed of without the certifier's authorisation (§ 193.005(g)). Inquest officers have the same five-day limit (§ 193.005(e)).

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate electronically with the local registrar within 10 days
steps.who: The person in charge of interment or of removal of the body from the registration district for disposition (the funeral director or person acting as one), who obtains the personal particulars from a competent person with knowledge of the facts.

deadline.text: not later than the 10th day after the date of death

steps.summary: The certificate is filed electronically, as the state registrar specifies, with the local registrar of the district where the death occurred or the body was found. Local registrars are justices of the peace (or the county clerk by agreement) and municipal clerks in towns of 2,500 or more. Failing to file is a Class C misdemeanor (§ 195.004).

steps.title: Report of death within 24 hours authorises in-state transport and burial; burial-transit permit for removal from the state, common carrier or cremation
steps.who: The funeral director who takes custody obtains an electronically filed report of death and transmits it to the local registrar; the local registrar, or the state registrar electronically, issues any burial-transit permit.
steps.trigger: Custody of the body by the funeral director; for the permit, presentation of a death certificate completed so far as possible.

deadline.text: report of death transmitted to the local registrar within 24 hours

steps.summary: Under the department's rule the report of death itself is the authority to transport or bury within Texas; a burial-transit permit is needed only to remove the body from the state, ship it by common carrier, or cremate it. The statute (§ 193.008) only recognises other states' permits and has the department prescribe the form. Cremation also waits 48 hours from death unless waived, and a body subject to inquest needs the inquest officer's certificate first.

steps.title: Local registrar sends registered certificates to the state registrar monthly
steps.who: The local registrar, to the state registrar (DSHS Vital Statistics Section).
steps.trigger: Certificates registered in the preceding month.

deadline.text: on the 10th day of each month

steps.summary: The statute still describes a monthly transmission of the original certificates (or a no-deaths report). With electronic filing the record is already in the state system; the statute does not say how the two interact.

steps.title: Certified copies to properly qualified applicants; death records public 25 years after death
steps.who: The state registrar, a local registrar or the county clerk.
steps.trigger: Application by a properly qualified applicant, with identification and fee.
steps.summary: Certified copies go only to a properly qualified applicant: the registrant, immediate family, guardian or legal representative, or others with a direct and tangible interest (25 TAC § 181.1). Under the Public Information Act a death record becomes public on the 25th anniversary of death (first anniversary if the decedent is unidentified).

steps.title: Local registrar files a monthly abstract of adult deaths with the county voter registrar and the Secretary of State
steps.who: The local registrar of deaths, to the voter registrar of the decedent's county of residence and to the Secretary of State.
steps.trigger: Death certificates issued in the month for Texas residents aged 18 or older.

deadline.text: abstract prepared each month and filed not later than the seventh day after it is prepared

steps.latencyNote: Each month … not later than the seventh day after the date the abstract is prepared (elec-16-001-a)
steps.summary: Filing with the Secretary of State must be electronic unless waived. The voter registrar cancels the registration immediately on receipt of the abstract (§ 16.031(a)(2)).

steps.title: State vital statistics unit sends death information to the Secretary of State weekly
steps.who: The DSHS vital statistics unit, to the Secretary of State, who periodically passes the information to county voter registrars.
steps.trigger: Every death certificate filed with a local registrar in Texas (county of residence, date of birth and full name at least, with matching identifiers under an MOU).

deadline.text: once each week, on a day specified by the secretary of state

steps.latencyNote: Once each week, on a day specified by the secretary of state (elec-16-001-c)
steps.summary: The feed supports the statewide voter registration list; a voter registrar who determines from it that a voter has died cancels the registration immediately (§ 16.031(b)(1)).

steps.title: Probate clerk files a monthly abstract of probate and heirship filings with the voter registrar and the Secretary of State
steps.who: The clerk of each court with probate jurisdiction.
steps.trigger: Applications for probate of a will, administration or determination of heirship, and small-estate affidavits, filed in the month.

deadline.text: abstract prepared each month and filed not later than the seventh day after it is prepared

steps.latencyNote: Each month … not later than the seventh day after the date the abstract is prepared (elec-16-001-b)
steps.summary: A second, court-side route to the voter roll; the registrar cancels on receipt (§ 16.031(a)(2)). It runs from the probate filing, not the death.

steps.title: Secretary of State obtains SSA death data quarterly
steps.who: The Secretary of State, from the Social Security Administration.
steps.trigger: Quarterly request by the Secretary of State.
steps.summary: The Secretary of State must go and get SSA's information on deceased Texas residents each quarter.

steps.title: Vital statistics provides death information to the Department of Public Safety for driver licence and ID records
steps.who: DSHS, to the Department of Public Safety, under a memorandum of understanding.
steps.latencyNote: an efficient and effective method to verify death information (hsc-191-010); no cadence in the statute
steps.summary: The MOU must include a mechanism for DSHS to provide death information with unique identifiers, including SSNs, to match driver's licence and ID records. The statute sets no frequency; the MOU itself was not read.

steps.title: Health and Human Services Commission matches vital statistics death records against Medicaid, TANF and SNAP rolls monthly
steps.who: The Health and Human Services Commission.
steps.summary: HHSC must each month match vital statistics death records against Medicaid eligibility and promptly remove the deceased (Gov't Code § 532.0201(e)), and do the same for TANF and SNAP benefits (§ 544.0456(c)). It is a match HHSC runs, so a pull.

steps.title: Vital statistics provides death information to Level I trauma hospitals for Medicaid managed care
steps.who: DSHS, to hospitals designated as Level I trauma facilities (and, subject to resources, other licensed hospitals).
steps.trigger: Every death certificate filed with a local registrar (county of residence, date of birth, full name at least).
steps.latencyNote: an efficient and effective procedure to provide death information (hsc-191-012); no cadence
steps.summary: Added in 2025 (S.B. 1467), effective 1 September 2025, to assist hospitals' participation in Medicaid managed care. The recipients are hospitals, which may be public or private; the statute sets no frequency.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Not later than the 10th day after the date of death (HSC § 193.003(a)).

informantDuty.note: The person in charge of interment or of removal of the body for disposition files (HSC § 193.002), i.e. the funeral director or person acting as one (25 TAC § 181.2); personal particulars come from a competent person with knowledge of the facts (§ 193.004).

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of every certificate: the attending physician, PA or APRN certifies (HSC § 193.005), and a justice of the peace or medical examiner acts only on reportable deaths (CCP arts. 49.04, 49.25). No review provision was found in HSC chs. 191-195.

electronicRegistration.note: The filer files the certificate electronically as specified by the state registrar (§ 193.002(4)) and certifiers attest through an approved electronic process (§ 193.005(h)). The system's name, TxEVER, is not in the statute.

centralPopulationRegister.note: Texas has no population register; death information is sent body by body from the vital statistics unit (voter roll, DPS, hospitals) or matched by HHSC.

governmentPropagation.note: Registration alone reaches the voter roll (monthly local abstracts and a weekly state feed, Elec. Code § 16.001), DPS licence records (HSC § 191.010) and HHSC's monthly Medicaid/TANF/SNAP matching (Gov't Code §§ 532.0201, 544.0456). SSA feeds are in the federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: Certified copies only to properly qualified applicants (HSC § 191.051; 25 TAC § 181.1); death records become public 25 years after death (Gov't Code § 552.115).

gaps: Rechecked 28 October 2026: statute text was read from the official chapter downloads (https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/Zips/<CODE>.htm.zip for HS, CR, EL, GV, listed in statutes.capitol.texas.gov/assets/StatuteCodeDownloads.json), because the public statutes.capitol.texas.gov pages are a client-rendered shell. Citations give the public Docs/<CODE>/htm/<CODE>.<ch>.htm#<section> address readers use. Every quote appears verbatim in those files.

First-pass errors corrected: § 193.005 is catchlined 'Personal information' but carries the medical-certification duty and a five-day deadline (the first pass left the deadline unknown); § 193.008 only recognises other states' burial-transit permits, and the in-state rule is 25 TAC § 181.2 (report of death within 24 hours is the authority to bury in Texas; a permit is needed only for removal from the state, common carrier or cremation); Election Code § 16.001(a) sends the local registrar's monthly abstract to the Secretary of State as well as the county voter registrar, within seven days of preparation; the weekly state feed is § 16.001(c) with HSC § 191.011.

Texas Administrative Code (25 TAC ch. 181) was read on www.law.cornell.edu, the mirror the schema allows, because texreg.sos.state.tx.us, www.sos.state.tx.us, www.sos.texas.gov and texas-sos.appianportalsgov.com are all egress-denied (CONNECT tunnel failed, 403). The Cornell copy carries Texas Register amendment notes through 24 November 2021 for § 181.2.

Code of Criminal Procedure chapter 49 is repealed and recodified as chapter 49A by H.B. 1610 (2025), effective 1 April 2027; steps cite the chapter in force now. HSC § 193.005(d)-(e) already carry both versions.

Not found in statute: the cadence of the DSHS-to-DPS death data (HSC § 191.010 delegates it to an MOU that was not read) and of the DSHS-to-hospital feed (§ 191.012). No statutory Texas feed to SSA was found in HSC title 3; SSA's EDR data exchange is a federal-layer matter.
www.dshs.texas.gov (Vital Statistics Section guidance, TxEVER) remains egress-denied, so the TxEVER system and fee schedules were not read.
privateSectorVerification is deliberately omitted so the us-federal value (LADMF) applies; Texas law adds only the hospital feed in HSC § 191.012.
